chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the minimum for which the thief’s hand is cut off. He said: “For an iron helmet.” I said: “And what is its price?” He said: “A quarter of a dīnār.”

And ʿAlī said, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The hand of the thief is not cut off until his theft reaches a quarter of a dīnār, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام did cut off [the hand] for an iron helmet.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose judicial action is cited as precedent
key_terms.بَيْضَةِ حَدِيدٍ: an iron helmet, cited as an example of the stolen item meeting the threshold
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ يَدُ: the legal cutting off of the hand as the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: a quarter of a dīnār, the minimum value required for amputation in this report
key_terms.سَرِقَتُهُ: the amount or value of what he stole
key_terms.ٱلسَّارِقُ: the thief who is subject to the legal ruling discussed here

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of theft for which a thief’s hand is cut off in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal threshold at which the hadd punishment for theft is applied. It identifies that the stolen amount must reach a quarter of a dīnār, illustrated by the example of an iron helmet, and it cites the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in this matter.
